subject: Action summary & first 30-day plan — Meridian Analytics initial eval
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: asha.mehta@meridiananalytics.com; tom.reynolds@meridiananalytics.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + proposal: 30-day pilot plan and immediate asks

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Short note to capture what we aligned on and propose an immediate 30-day plan so we can get to a meaningful signal quickly. TL;DR: focus on query-gen latency and hallucination reduction for your insights product; pilot scope targets throughput at 200 QPM and <350ms median token latency with automatic prefix cache enabled.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: high per-query cost and inconsistent latency when analysts hit long-context queries (>3k tokens).
- Quality concern: hallucination on revenue attribution queries, especially when data slices are sparse.
- Goal: reduce cost-per-query by ~40% while maintaining or improving factual accuracy measured on your 150-item prompt test-set.

Proposed 30-day pilot scope (minimal, measurable)
1) Dataset + access: Meridian provides a 2-week sample (S3) of anonymized logs and a 150-prompt eval set (we discussed urgent subset of 50 prompts).
2) Model/config: run two candidate model configs (quantized LlamaX-3b + Redwood-lv2-7b fallback) with caching & tuned batching.
3) Metrics: latency (p50/p95), cost/token, hallucination rate on eval set, throughput (QPM). Success threshold: 40% cost reduction or >=20% latency improvement with <=5% regression on accuracy.
4) Owners: Lauren (engaged owner / success metrics), Ben (ops & infra), Asha (Meridian product lead), Tom (data eng).
5) Kickoff timeline: access + sample data by 2026-10-22; infra standing config by 2026-10-26; first eval run by 2026-10-30; review and decision by 2026-11-05.

Immediate asks from Meridian (what we need to start)
- A sample S3 path or CSV export (logs) + IAM role or pre-signed URLs (small sample OK).
- The 150-prompt eval set (or first 50 for an initial pass).
- Contact for procurement (PO/finance) for a short reserved capacity commitment if results look good.

Attachments: redwood-poc-metrics-template.xlsx (basic metric sheet) and access-checklist-sample.txt.

Next steps
- Asha: share sample data & who owns S3 / credentials by Thu 10/22.
- Ben: I'll spin up the sandbox infra and share endpoints by 10/26.
- Lauren: I'll run the initial eval, share results and cost breakdown after the run (expected 10/30).

Happy to adjust scope — if you'd prefer we prioritize hallucination reduction experiments first, we can swap the order.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

- For eval prompts: we will upload the full 150-set but will mark an initial 50 as high-priority (revenue attribution examples).
- Procurement: our buyer is Claire Nguyen (claire.nguyen@meridiananalytics.com), CC'd on future procurement threads. They prefer a 30-day trial invoice / short-term contract for proof-of-value.

We will aim to deliver the S3 presigned URLs and the prompt set by 10/22. Could you confirm the minimum IAM permissions you need to read the sample? Also, please share the sandbox endpoint and any IP allowlist info so our infra team can approve network egress if needed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround, and excited to see the initial numbers.
